anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, references D10 (CAN0) and D9 (CAN1) are drawn as dual-channel optocouplers (LED input + phototransistor output symbol with optical arrows) inserted in the CAN differential pair between the transceiver CANH/CANL pins (U11/U10) and the M12 connectors J2/J13 (nets CAN0_P/CAN0_N, CAN1_P/CAN1_N). No CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode array appears anywhere on the CAN nets; the only TVS parts on the board are TPD4E1U06DCKR (Ethernet) and USBLC6-2P6 (USB).
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table states D9/D10 are CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N and CAN1_P/N providing CAN bus transient/ESD protection, and that U11 is already an isolated CAN transceiver. Optocouplers belong neither in the differential CAN pair nor in place of the documented TVS arrays.

evidence.quote: D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N | CAN bus transient/ESD protection ... the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice.
CAN BUS sheet: U11 CANH/CANL -> D10 (optocoupler symbol, 'Input'/'Output') -> CAN0_P/CAN0_N to J2; U10 -> D9 -> CAN1_P/CAN1_N to J13; no SM712 part present on these nets.

anomalies.impact: The CAN buses lose their specified ESD/transient protection, and placing slow single-ended optocouplers in the high-speed differential CAN pair corrupts/attenuates the signaling, likely rendering CAN0/CAN1 non-functional or unreliable against motor-controller traffic.

parsed.summary: The CAN protection path deviates from the intended design: the spec-mandated CDSOT23-SM712 TVS arrays on D9/D10 are absent and those references instead carry dual optocouplers wired into the CAN0/CAN1 differential pairs, removing ESD protection and corrupting the CAN signaling.
